rows.jp: 壁に寄りかかって所在なげにしている美希と遭遇。
rows.en: I ran into Miki leaning against a wall with nothing to do.

ghs.en: A random encounter with Miki leaning against the wall, idling.

rows.jp: 美希は見た感じ、それほどショックを受けていない。
rows.en: Miki did not look terribly shaken.

ghs.en: The impression that I got from looking at Miki was that she was not particularly shocked by all this.

rows.jp: そう振る舞っているのだろうけど。
rows.en: Though perhaps she was only putting on a brave face.

ghs.en: But it's probably her just acting like that.

rows.jp: 「は、部活のおかげでなんとか」
rows.en: “Y-yeah. I’m managing somehow, thanks to the club.”

ghs.assessment: The initial は is a hesitant filler. 'Sah!' invents a forceful exclamation, while 'thanks to club' lacks the article or possessive required in English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Uh, somehow—thanks to the club.'

highlights.text: Miki: "Sah! Thanks to club, somehow."

ghs.assessment: もういっこの部活 refers to the other club. 'That one more club' treats it as an additional count and is not grammatical English.
ghs.remedy: Use '...The other club, you mean.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...that one more club innit."

rows.jp: 正式名称・生命維持活動部だ。
rows.en: Its official name was the Life-Support Activities Club.

ghs.en: Formal name: Life Maintenance and Improvement Club.
ghs.assessment: The formal name is 生命維持活動部, the Life Maintenance Activities Club. 'Improvement' is not present in the name and changes the club's stated function.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Its formal name is the Life Maintenance Activities Club.'

highlights.text: Formal name: Life Maintenance and Improvement Club.

rows.jp: 「……霧ちんも参加してるんだよな」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...Kiri-chin's also a member there, right."

rows.jp: 「先輩が参加してないのが不思議ですね」
rows.en: “It’s strange that you aren’t taking part, Taichi.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Very strange that you are not participating, Senpai."
ghs.assessment: 不思議ですね expresses mild wonder that the addressee is not participating. 'Very strange' adds degree and makes the judgment harsher.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's odd that you aren't participating, Senpai.'

highlights.text: Miki: "Very strange that you are not participating, Senpai."

rows.jp: 「んー、そら君。霧ちんは俺のこと―――」
rows.en: “Well, you see, Miki. Kiri thinks of me as―――”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ngh, c'mon you. Kiri-chin and me, we---"
ghs.assessment: そら君 is a colloquial lead-in equivalent to 'well, that's because.' 'C'mon you' addresses Miki as an objector, while 'Kiri-chin and me, we' supplies a reciprocal construction before the source sentence is interrupted.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Well, that's because Kiri-chin thinks of me—'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ngh, c'mon you. Kiri-chin and me, we---"

rows.jp: と話していると、霧ちんがトイレから出てきた。
rows.en: As we spoke, Kiri emerged from the restroom.

ghs.en: And on talking about her, Kiri-chin came out of the toilet.
ghs.assessment: と話していると means 'while we were talking' or 'as we said this.' 'On talking about her' explicitly makes Kiri the topic and adds a coincidence formula absent from the Japanese.
ghs.remedy: Use 'As we were talking, Kiri-chin came out of the restroom.'

highlights.text: And on talking about her, Kiri-chin came out of the toilet.

rows.jp: 「きききき禁断の問いをーっ！？」

ghs.en: Kiri seems to have a bit of bruxism.
ghs.assessment: The source directly says Kiri ground her teeth. 'Seems to have a bit of bruxism' turns the visible action into a tentative medical diagnosis and adds minimization.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Kiri ground her teeth.'

highlights.text: Kiri seems to have a bit of bruxism.

rows.en: So we were dispensing with the courtesies.
And treating me like her mortal enemy.

ghs.en: And treated like a sworn enemy as well?

rows.jp: 冷たいまなざしを向けてくる。
rows.en: She fixed me with an icy stare.

ghs.en: A frosty look was turned towards me.
ghs.assessment: The source uses active present narration: she directs a cold gaze at the narrator. The passive past 'was turned towards me' is both temporally inconsistent and unnecessarily calqued.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She fixes me with a cold stare.'

highlights.text: A frosty look was turned towards me.

rows.jp: 霧も相変わらず、いつも通りのままだった。
rows.en: Kiri, too, was the same as ever.

ghs.en: Ever unchanging Kiri, always in the same way she was.
ghs.assessment: The English repeats the same idea in 'ever unchanging' and 'always in the same way,' then ends with an unstable past clause. The source simply notes that Kiri remains her usual self.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Kiri, too, was unchanged—the same as ever.'

highlights.text: Ever unchanging Kiri, always in the same way she was.

rows.en: That was something of a relief.

ghs.assessment: ちょっと安心 is the narrator's reaction of feeling a little relieved. 'Ease up a little!' converts it into an imperative addressed to someone else.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That is a little reassuring.'

highlights.text: Ease up a little!

rows.jp: 「霧や、あいかわらず美しい肌だ」
rows.en: “Kiri, your skin is as lovely as ever.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Kiri, as always such a lovely skin you have."
ghs.assessment: Skin is normally uncountable in this construction. 'Such a lovely skin you have' is unidiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Kiri, your skin is as lovely as ever.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Kiri, as always such a lovely skin you have."

rows.jp: 手の甲でしなやかに撃墜された。
rows.en: She gracefully shot it down with the back of her hand.

ghs.en: The back of her hand supplely shoots me down.
ghs.assessment: The source says the extended hand or finger is nimbly knocked down with the back of her hand. 'Supplely' is not standard English, while 'shoots me down' changes a physical parry into rejection of the person.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She deftly knocks it aside with the back of her hand.'

highlights.text: The back of her hand supplely shoots me down.

ghs.assessment: 前髪を払う is the narrator brushing his bangs aside. 'Sweep my bangs' does not state the directional action and can suggest sweeping the hair itself away.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I brush my bangs aside.'

highlights.text: I sweep my bangs.

rows.jp: 「あわわ、けんかしちゃだめですよ」

ghs.assessment: The source is childishly flustered but grammatical. 'Quarreling is no go' is broken English, and 'AhWahWah' is not a controlled rendering of the opening vocalization.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A-awawa, you mustn't fight!'

highlights.text: Miki: "AhWahWah, quarreling is no go!"

rows.jp: 「喧嘩など、そんな野蛮なことはしないさ」
rows.en: “Fighting? I would never do anything so uncivilized.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I would never do something as uncivilized as quarreling."

rows.jp: 「もっと優美に決闘といきたいものだ」
rows.en: “I would prefer a more elegant duel.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I would prefer something more refined, like a duel."

rows.jp: 「……それってわたしに勝負をふっかけるということですか、先輩？」
rows.en: “……Are you challenging me to a duel, Taichi?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...do you mean to provoke me into a game, Senpai?"
ghs.assessment: 勝負をふっかける means to challenge someone to a contest or fight. 'Provoke me into a game' changes the action and narrows 勝負 to play.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Does that mean you're challenging me, Senpai?'

highlights.text: Kiri: "...do you mean to provoke me into a game, Senpai?"

rows.en: “Hmm. If it were a duel by night.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Indeed. It is a Duel of the Night."
ghs.assessment: 夜の決闘であれば is a conditional offer: 'if it is a duel at night.' The English turns it into a present declaration and invents a title-like capitalization.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Mm. If it is a duel at night.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Indeed. It is a Duel of the Night."

rows.jp: 霧は美希の腕を引いて、踵を返した。
rows.en: Kiri grabbed Miki by the arm and turned on her heel.

ghs.en: Kiri pulled Miki's arm and spun on her heels.

rows.en: “Let’s go, let’s go! The nerve of him!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Go let's go, apologies for the intrusion, yes!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese speaker and feminine complaint identify Kiri as the one urging Miki onward. The English labels Taichi as speaker and then renders the exasperated complaint as an apology for intruding.
ghs.remedy: Attribute the line to Kiri and use 'Come on, Miki. Honestly, the nerve of him!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Go let's go, apologies for the intrusion, yes!"

ghs.assessment: 並んだ says the narrator falls into step or lines up alongside the departing pair. 'I line up' sounds like entering a queue and misses the carried movement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I fall into step beside them.'

highlights.text: I line up.

rows.jp: 三人はとっても仲良し。
rows.en: The three of us were the best of friends.

ghs.en: The three of them really go well together.
ghs.assessment: The source mockingly declares the three participants very close. 'The three of them' excludes the first-person narrator, while 'go well together' evaluates compatibility rather than closeness.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The three of us are the best of friends.'

highlights.text: The three of them really go well together.

rows.jp: 菜の花を思わせる、華やか三姉妹！
rows.en: Three radiant sisters, bright as a field of golden mustard blossoms!

ghs.en: Three gay sisters that remind of rapeseed blossoms!
ghs.assessment: 華やか means glamorous, splendid, or brilliant, not 'gay' in the modern English sense. 'That remind of' is also missing the required object or subject construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Three radiant sisters, reminiscent of rapeseed blossoms!'

highlights.text: Three gay sisters that remind of rapeseed blossoms!

rows.jp: これはそんな三人娘の、うつくしい愛の物語♪
rows.en: A beautiful tale of love shared by three girls♪

ghs.en: And this is the story of these three girls, a beautiful tale of love!♪

rows.jp: 「気づかないのは脳みその軽い先輩だけです」
rows.en: “You’re the only one empty-headed enough not to notice, Taichi.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "The only one who has not noticed is Senpai with his lightweight brain matter."

rows.jp: 「ぶちまけてみないとわからないですけどね」
rows.en: “We won’t know until I splatter it, will we?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "But unless I speak candidly you do not understand, it seems."
ghs.assessment: ぶちまける continues the brain-color exchange with the violent image of spilling the contents out to inspect them. 'Speak candidly' selects an unrelated idiom and destroys the threat and callback.
ghs.remedy: Use 'We won't know unless I splatter it out and take a look.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "But unless I speak candidly you do not understand, it seems."

rows.jp: 「……こんな状況で、脳天気なもんですね」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...thoughtlessly optimistic even in this situation I see."
ghs.assessment: 脳天気 means carefree or obliviously cheerful. 'Thoughtlessly optimistic even in this situation I see' is not grammatical dialogue and changes the trait into an adverbial judgment.
ghs.remedy: Use '...You're awfully carefree in a situation like this.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "...thoughtlessly optimistic even in this situation I see."

rows.jp: 「いやなに、そう誉めるな。照れちゃうではないか」
rows.en: “Come now, don’t praise me so. You’ll make me blush.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Naaah, now, please, not all that praise. You want me to go all red in the face?"
ghs.assessment: The source jokes that such praise will make the speaker blush. 'You want me to go all red in the face?' changes the result into an accusation about the addressee's desire.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Oh, come now, don't praise me so much. You'll make me blush.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Naaah, now, please, not all that praise. You want me to go all red in the face?"

rows.jp: 「でもわたし、知ってます。だから」

ghs.en: Kiri: "But I know, and well. Therefore."
ghs.assessment: でもわたし、知ってます。だから is a hesitant transition: 'But I know. So...' 'But I know, and well. Therefore.' is not coherent English and makes the unfinished thought falsely formal.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But I know. So...'

highlights.text: Kiri: "But I know, and well. Therefore."

ghs.assessment: ほえ is a comic vocalization. 'Whaet' reads as an accidental transposition rather than a legible sound rendering.
ghs.remedy: Use a consistent reaction such as 'Huh?' or 'Wha...?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Whaet?"

rows.jp: 「絶対に気を許すつもりはありませんから」
rows.en: “I will never let my guard down around you.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Therefore I have no intention of letting my guard down."

rows.en: The two of them walked away.

ghs.assessment: なんだろう is the narrator wondering what to make of the exchange or atmosphere. 'Really now' is an exasperated judgment rather than a question of interpretation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What was that about?'

highlights.text: Really now.

rows.jp: あの切迫した……雰囲気は。

ghs.en: Too much... tension in this air.

rows.jp: 両名の背中に呼びかける。

ghs.en: I call out towards the backs of both.

rows.jp: 立ち止まり、振り向いたのは美希だけだったが。
rows.en: They stopped, though only Miki turned around.

ghs.en: Stops in her tracks and turns around, however, Miki alone.
ghs.assessment: The source states that only Miki stopped and turned around. 'Stops in her tracks and turns around, however, Miki alone' is a subject-delayed fragment with broken word order.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Only Miki stopped and turned around.'

highlights.text: Stops in her tracks and turns around, however, Miki alone.

ghs.assessment: 言いよどむ is a complete first-person action. 'Fumbling for the right words' is an unattached participial fragment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I falter.'

highlights.text: Fumbling for the right words.

rows.jp: 「くれぐれも体調には気をつけるんだぞ」
rows.en: “Take good care of yourselves, all right?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Be thoroughly careful with your physical conditions!"
ghs.assessment: 体調 is health or physical condition in the singular collective sense. 'Be thoroughly careful with your physical conditions' is an unnatural plural calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Take very good care of yourselves.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Be thoroughly careful with your physical conditions!"

ghs.assessment: 無難なところ means that this is the safe, inoffensive thing to say. 'A refuge in safety' invents a physical or metaphorical shelter.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A safe enough thing to say.'

highlights.text: A refuge in safety.

rows.jp: 確かに文明と切り離された今、体調管理は切実だしな。
rows.en: Cut off from civilization as we were, staying healthy really was an urgent concern.

ghs.en: Certainly, as we are cut off from civilization now, managing physical condition is paramount.

rows.jp: 美希が元気良く挙手し、霧がちらりと目線を流した。
rows.en: Miki shot a hand into the air; Kiri flicked a glance back.

ghs.en: Miki gave a vigorous salute, Kiri shed but a peeking glance.
ghs.assessment: 美希が元気良く挙手する means Miki energetically raises her hand, not that she salutes. ちらりと目線を流す is Kiri casting a brief glance, not 'shedding' one.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Miki raises her hand energetically, and Kiri casts me a brief glance.'

highlights.text: Miki gave a vigorous salute, Kiri shed but a peeking glance.
